{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01ADi9DwZccDMkjKJSbzEYF4","type":"tool_result","content":"=== app_server/__init__.py\n\"\"\"Flask application factory for the ReadingList web application.\"\"\"\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom flask import Flask\n\nfrom persistence import open_database\n\nfrom .books import bp as books_bp\nfrom .settings import Settings\n\nTEMPLATE_FOLDER = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / \"templates\"\n\n\ndef create_app() -> Flask:\n    \"\"\"Build and return the ReadingList Flask application.\n\n    Opening the store does not connect to it; connections are made on first use, per thread.\n    \"\"\"\n    settings = Settings.from_environment()\n    app = Flask(__name__, template_folder=str(TEMPLATE_FOLDER))\n    app.extensions[\"database\"] = open_database(settings.database_url)\n    app.register_blueprint(books_bp)\n    return app\n=== app_server/books.py\n\"\"\"HTTP routes for books: add a book from a form post.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom flask import Blueprint, current_app, redirect, render_template, request\nfrom werkzeug.wrappers import Response\n\nfrom persistence import Database\n\nfrom .book_service import BookRejected, add_book\n\nbp = Blueprint(\"books\", __name__)\n\n\ndef _database() -> Database:\n    return current_app.extensions[\"database\"]\n\n\n@bp.post(\"/books\")\ndef create_book() -> Response:\n    \"\"\"Add a book from the ``title`` and ``author`` form fields, then redirect to the start page.\"\"\"\n    title = request.form.get(\"title\", \"\").strip()\n    author = request.form.get(\"author\", \"\").strip()\n    try:\n        add_book(_database(), title=title, author=author)\n    except BookRejected as rejected:\n        return Response(\n            render_template(\"base.html\", error=rejected.reason),\n            status=400,\n            mimetype=\"text/html\",\n        )\n    return redirect(\"/\", code=303)\n=== app_server/book_service.py\n\"\"\"Book behavior for the ReadingList web application, free of any Flask dependency.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom persistence import Database\nfrom persistence.schema import BookRow\n\n\nclass BookRejected(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"A submission the application refuses to store; ``reason`` says why.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, reason: str) -> None:\n        super().__init__(reason)\n        self.reason = reason\n\n\ndef add_book(database: Database, title: str, author: str) -> BookRow:\n    \"\"\"Store a book appended after every existing book and return the stored row.\n\n    Values are expected already trimmed by the caller. An empty title or author is refused\n    without touching the store, so a stored book always has both.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not title:\n        raise BookRejected(\"rejected: title is empty\")\n    if not author:\n        raise BookRejected(\"rejected: author is empty\")\n    return database.books.create(title=title, author=author)\n=== app_server/settings.py\n\"\"\"Typed runtime settings for the ReadingList web application.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nDEFAULT_DATABASE_PATH = \"data/app.db\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Settings:\n    \"\"\"Runtime settings read from the environment.\"\"\"\n\n    database_url: str\n\n    @classmethod\n    def from_environment(cls) -> Settings:\n        \"\"\"Read DATABASE_URL, then DATABASE_PATH, then fall back to the default store path.\"\"\"\n        configured = (\n            os.environ.get(\"DATABASE_URL\") or os.environ.get(\"DATABASE_PATH\") or DEFAULT_DATABASE_PATH\n        )\n        return cls(database_url=configured)\n=== app_server/testing.py\n\"\"\"Test helpers for the ReadingList web application.\"\"\"\n\nfrom flask.testing import FlaskClient\n\nfrom app_server import create_app\n\n\ndef web_client() -> FlaskClient:\n    \"\"\"Return a Flask test client for a fresh application with TESTING enabled.\"\"\"\n    app = create_app()\n    app.config[\"TESTING\"] = True\n    return app.test_client()\n=== bin/run.sh\n#!/bin/sh\n# ReadingList development server launcher.\n# Activates the project .venv and starts Flask with the application factory.\nset -eu\n\nPROJECT_DIR=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")/..\" && pwd)\"\ncd \"$PROJECT_DIR\"\n\nif [ ! -f .venv/bin/activate ]; then\n    echo \"error: .venv is missing. Run 'uv sync' from the application root first.\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\n. .venv/bin/activate\nexec flask --app app_server:create_app run \"$@\"\n=== pyproject.toml\n[project]\nname = \"readinglist\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\nrequires-python = \">=3.11\"\ndependencies = [\n    \"flask>=3.1.3\",\n]\n\n[dependency-groups]\ndev = [\n    \"pytest>=9.0.3\",\n]\n\n[tool.pytest.ini_options]\ntestpaths = [\"tests\"]\npythonpath = [\".\"]\n=== .gitignore\n.venv/\n__pycache__/\n.pytest_cache/\ndata/\n.env\n=== tests/conftest.py\n\"\"\"Shared pytest fixtures for the ReadingList test suite.\"\"\"\n\nfrom collections.abc import Iterator\n\nimport pytest\nfrom flask.testing import make_client\n\n    return make_client()\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef db_session() -> Iterator[object]:\n    \"\"\"Provide a rolled-back database session from the generated persistence package.\n\n    The persistence package is generated from DATABASE.md at the DATABASE build step,\n    so the import is deferred until a test requests this fixture.\n    \"\"\"\n    from persistence.testing import db_session as open_session\n\n    with open_session() as db:\n        yield db\n=== tests/test_add_book.py\n\"\"\"Add a book: POST /books stores a valid submission and redirects to the start page.\"\"\"\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom app_server import create_app\nfrom app_server.book_service import BookRejected, add_book\n\nPROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef app(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n    \"\"\"A fresh application over its own store, so no test touches the configured data/app.db.\"\"\"\n    store = tmp_path / \"add-book.db\"\n    monkeypatch.setenv(\"DATABASE_URL\", f\"sqlite:///{store}\")\n    monkeypatch.delenv(\"DATABASE_PATH\", raising=False)\n    application = create_app()\n    application.extensions[\"database\"].execute_script((PROJECT_ROOT / \"schema.sql\").read_text())\n    return application\n\n\ndef _stored(app) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Read every stored book back through the persistence package, in order added.\"\"\"\n    return [(row.title, row.author) for row in app.extensions[\"database\"].books.list()]\n\n\ndef test_valid_submission_redirects_with_303_to_start_page(app):\n    response = app.test_client().post(\"/books\", data={\"title\": \"Dune\", \"author\": \"Frank Herbert\"})\n\n    assert response.status_code == 303\n    assert response.headers[\"Location\"] == \"/\"\n\n\ndef test_valid_submission_stores_title_and_author(app):\n    app.test_client().post(\"/books\", data={\"title\": \"Dune\", \"author\": \"Frank Herbert\"})\n\n    assert _stored(app) == [(\"Dune\", \"Frank Herbert\")]\n\n\ndef test_surrounding_whitespace_is_trimmed_before_storing(app):\n    app.test_client().post(\"/books\", data={\"title\": \"  Dune \\t\", \"author\": \"\\n Frank Herbert  \"})\n\n    assert _stored(app) == [(\"Dune\", \"Frank Herbert\")]\n\n\ndef test_internal_whitespace_is_kept(app):\n    app.test_client().post(\"/books\", data={\"title\": \"Dune  Messiah\", \"author\": \"Frank  Herbert\"})\n\n    assert _stored(app) == [(\"Dune  Messiah\", \"Frank  Herbert\")]\n\n\ndef test_new_book_is_appended_after_existing_books(app):\n    client = app.test_client()\n    client.post(\"/books\", data={\"title\": \"First\", \"author\": \"A\"})\n    client.post(\"/books\", data={\"title\": \"Second\", \"author\": \"B\"})\n    client.post(\"/books\", data={\"title\": \"Third\", \"author\": \"C\"})\n\n    assert _stored(app) == [(\"First\", \"A\"), (\"Second\", \"B\"), (\"Third\", \"C\")]\n\n\ndef test_same_book_submitted_twice_is_stored_twice(app):\n    client = app.test_client()\n    client.post(\"/books\", data={\"title\": \"Dune\", \"author\": \"Frank Herbert\"})\n    client.post(\"/books\", data={\"title\": \"Dune\", \"author\": \"Frank Herbert\"})\n\n    assert _stored(app) == [(\"Dune\", \"Frank Herbert\"), (\"Dune\", \"Frank Herbert\")]\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    \"form\",\n    [\n        {\"title\": \"\", \"author\": \"Frank Herbert\"},\n        {\"title\": \"   \", \"author\": \"Frank Herbert\"},\n        {\"title\": \"Dune\", \"author\": \"\"},\n        {\"title\": \"Dune\", \"author\": \" \\t \"},\n        {\"title\": \"\", \"author\": \"\"},\n        {\"author\": \"Frank Herbert\"},\n        {\"title\": \"Dune\"},\n        {},\n    ],\n    ids=[\n        \"empty-title\",\n        \"blank-title\",\n        \"empty-author\",\n        \"blank-author\",\n        \"both-empty\",\n b\"rejected: author is empty\" in response.data\n\n\ndef test_rejection_after_valid_submission_keeps_earlier_book(app):\n    client = app.test_client()\n    client.post(\"/books\", data={\"title\": {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01LZ3MBv8g1o2rL8D7tHj2Fz","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"Persistence for this Target. Shipped engines plus the schema generated from DATABASE.md.\"\"\"\n\nfrom .db import Database, PersistenceError, UnknownOperation\nfrom .schema import SCHEMA, open_database\n\n__all__ = [\"Database\", \"PersistenceError\", \"SCHEMA\", \"UnknownOperation\", \"open_database\"]\n\"\"\"Persistence access for a Drydock Target.\n\nThis file is shipped by Drydock and copied into the build unchanged. Do not edit it here: edit\n``DATABASE.md`` and rebuild. It is hardened and tested once, in Drydock's own suite, so every\nTarget inherits a persistence layer that has already passed rather than one re-derived from prose\non each build.\n\nThe application-facing surface is ``Database``. One attribute per declared table, one method per\ndeclared access pattern::\n\n    db = Database(dsn, SCHEMA)\n    ticket = db.tickets.get(id=7)\n    open_tickets = db.tickets.list(status=\"open\")\n\n``schema.py`` beside this file is generated from ``DATABASE.md`` and carries the tables, the\noperations, and the row types. It contains no SQL. Statements are constructed here, by the driver\nfor the engine in use, so a parameter placeholder never appears in generated code or in a caller.\n\nValues reach the database as bound parameters, never as formatted text. Identifiers cannot be\nbound in any engine, so they are taken only from the generated schema — which Drydock validated\nagainst ``^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`` before emitting it — and are quoted on the way out.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Mapping, Sequence\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, fields\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager\nimport threading\nfrom typing import Any\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"Database\",\n    \"Driver\",\n    \"Operation\",\n    \"PersistenceError\",\n    \"Schema\",\n    \"Table\",\n    \"statements\",\n    \"UnknownOperation\",\n]\n\nVERBS = (\"get\", \"list\", \"create\", \"update\", \"delete\")\n\n\nclass PersistenceError(RuntimeError):\n    \"\"\"A persistence failure the caller may act on, raised in place of a driver exception.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass UnknownOperation(PersistenceError):\n    \"\"\"A verb was requested that the declaration does not grant for that table.\"\"\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Table:\n    \"\"\"One declared table: its columns and the column that identifies a row.\"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    columns: tuple[str, ...]\n    primary_key: str | None = None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Operation:\n    \"\"\"One declared access pattern, reduced to what executing it requires.\n\n    ``inputs`` are the parameters the caller supplies; for ``get``, ``list``, and ``delete`` they\n    are the predicate, and for ``create`` and ``update`` they are the values written. ``row`` is\n    the dataclass a read or a create returns, and ``columns`` are the columns it selects.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    identifier: str\n    table: str\n    verb: str\n    inputs: tuple[str, ...]\n    row: type | None = None\n    columns: tuple[str, ...] = ()\n    key: str | None = None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Schema:\n    \"\"\"The generated declaration: every table and every operation reaching one.\"\"\"\n\n    tables: tuple[Table, ...]\n    operations: tuple[Operation, ...]\n\n    def by_table(self) -> dict[str, tuple[Operation, ...]]:\n        grouped: dict[str, list[Operation]] = {table.name: [] for table in self.tables}\n        for operation in self.operations:\n            grouped.setdefault(operation.table, []).append(operation)\n        return {name: tuple(items) for name, items in grouped.items()}\n\n\nclass Driver:\n    \"\"\"Statement construction shared by every engine.\n\n    Subclasses supply connection handling and the two things engines genuinely disagree about:\n    how a parameter is spelled, and how a freshly inserted row reports its key. Everything else is\n    identical SQL, so it is written once here rather than twice in the engines.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def prepare_schema(self, sql: str) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Translate generated DDL for this engine.\"\"\"\n        return sql\n\n    #: Spelled by the DB-API driver, not by this class's callers.\n    paramstyle = \"qmark\"\n    returning = False\n\n    def connect(self) -> Any:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def close(self) -> None:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def placeholder(self, index: int) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Render parameter ``index`` (0-based) in this engine's spelling.\"\"\"\n        return \"?\" if self.paramstyle == \"qmark\" else \"%s\"\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def quote(identifier: str) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Quote a declared identifier. Never called with caller-supplied text.\"\"\"\n        if not identifier.replace(\"_\", \"\").isalnum():\n            raise PersistenceError(f\"refusing unsafe identifier {identifier!r}\")\n        return f'\"{identifier}\"'\n\n    def _predicate(self, names: Sequence[str], start: int = 0) -> str:\n        return \" AND \".join(\n            f\"{self.quote(name)} = {self.placeholder(start + offset)}\"\n            for offset, name in enumerate(names)\n        )\n\n    def select(self, table: str, columns: Sequence[str], predicate: Sequence[str]) -> str:\n        selected = \", \".join(self.quote(name) for name in columns)\n        statement = f\"SELECT {selected} FROM {self.quote(table)}\"\n        if predicate:\n            statement += f\" WHERE {self._predicate(predicate)}\"\n        return statement\n\n    def insert(self, table: str, columns: Sequence[str], key: str | None) -> str:\n        names = \", \".join(self.quote(name) for name in columns)\n        marks = \", \".join(self.placeholder(index) for index in range(len(columns)))\n        statement = f\"INSERT INTO {self.quote(table)} ({names}) VALUES ({marks})\"\n        if self.returning and key:\n            statement += f\" RETURNING {self.quote(key)}\"\n        return statement\n\n    def update(self, table: str, columns: Sequence[str], predicate: Sequence[str]) -> str:\n        assignments = \", \".join(\n            f\"{self.quote(name)} = {self.placeholder(index)}\" for index, name in enumerate(columns)\n        )\n        statement = f\"UPDATE {self.quote(table)} SET {assignments}\"\n        if predicate:\n            statement += f\" WHERE {self._predicate(predicate, len(columns))}\"\n        return statement\n\n    def delete(self, table: str, predicate: Sequence[str]) -> str:\n        statement = f\"DELETE FROM {self.quote(table)}\"\n        if predicate:\n            statement += f\" WHERE {self._predicate(predicate)}\"\n        return statement\n\n    def inserted_key(self, cursor: Any) -> Any:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n\nclass TableAccess:\n    \"\"\"The methods one table grants, bound from the declaration rather than defined by hand.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, table: Table, operations: Iterable[Operation], database: Database) -> None:\n        self._table = table\n        self._database = database\n        self._operations = {operation.verb: operation for operation in operations}\n\n    def __repr__(self) -> str:\n        granted = \", \".join(sorted(self._operations))\n        return f\"<TableAccess {self._table.name}: {granted or 'no declared operation'}>\"\n\n    def __getattr__(self, verb: str) -> Callable[..., Any]:\n        operation = self._operations.get(verb)\n        if operation is None:\n            granted = \", \".join(sorted(self._operations)) or \"none\"\n            raise UnknownOperation(\n                f\"{self._table.name} declares no {verb!r} operation. Declared: {granted}. \"\n                \"Add an access pattern to DATABASE.md rather than reaching around this class.\"\n            )\n        return lambda **arguments: self._database.run(operation, arguments)\n\n\nclass Database:\n    \"\"\"One store, presented to callers as declared tables with declared methods.\n\n    Callers construct one instance, share it freely, and call methods synchronously. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01H26XPZP4kkqDCtQ7TWgTEv","type":"tool_result","content":"# FEATURE: List Books Tests\n\n| Field | Value |\n|-------|-------|\n| Version | 20261023 V1 |\n| Description | Automated pytest tests that prove books are listed in the order they were added. |\n| Depends On | FEATURE-ListBooks.md |\n| Provides | None |\n| Consumes | GET /books |\n\n## Purpose\n\nGuarantee that listing books in the order added is covered by an automated test that runs under `pytest -q`.\n\n## Deliverable\n\n`tests/test_list_books.py`, using the `web_client` fixture from `tests/conftest.py`. The file contains pytest tests covering at least:\n\n- an empty store returns an empty JSON array from `GET /books` (the test isolates its own data from any residue);\n- a single added book is returned with `id`, `title`, and `author`;\n- several books added in sequence are returned in the order added, with ascending ids.\n\nEach test uses unique titles and removes the books it created.\n\n## Reads\n\n`GET /books`.\n\n## Writes\n\n`POST /books`, as test setup only.\n\n## Database Interface\n\n- None — persistence is owned by FEATURE-ListBooks.md.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC list-tests-file-defines-tests ===\nIntent: tests/test_list_books.py exists, parses, defines at least three test functions, and exercises the books route.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: python-package=pytest; scope=test\n\nimport ast\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\npath = Path(\"tests/test_list_books.py\")\nassert path.is_file()\nsource = path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\ntree = ast.parse(source)\nnames = [\n    node.name\n    for node in ast.walk(tree)\n    if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)) and node.name.startswith(\"test_\")\n]\nassert len(names) >= 3\nassert \"/books\" in source\n=== END AC list-tests-file-defines-tests ===\n\n=== AC list-tests-pass ===\nIntent: The list-books test file passes when run with pytest from the application root.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: python-package=pytest; scope=test\n\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\n\nresult = subprocess.run(\n    [sys.executable, \"-m\", \"pytest\", \"-q\", \"tests/test_list_books.py\"],\n    capture_output=True,\n    text=True,\n)\nprint(result.stdout)\nprint(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr)\nassert result.returncode == 0\n=== END AC list-tests-pass ===\n\n=== AC list-order-behavior ===\nIntent: Books added in sequence are returned by GET /books in the order added.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: python-package=pytest; scope=test\n\nfrom app_server.testing import web_client\nfrom persistence.testing import committed_session\n\nauthor = \"ListTestsOrderAuthor\"\ntitles = [\"ListTestsFirst\", \"ListTestsSecond\", \"ListTestsThird\"]\n\n\ndef purge():\n    with committed_session() as db:\n        for row in db.books.list():\n            if row.author == author:\n                db.books.delete(id=row.id)\n\n\nclient = web_client()\npurge()\ntry:\n    for t in titles:\n        assert client.post(\"/books\", data={\"title\": t, \"author\": author}).status_code == 303\n    rows = [r for r in client.get(\"/books\").get_json() if r[\"author\"] == author]\n    assert [r[\"title\"] for r in rows] == titles\n    ids = [r[\"id\"] for r in rows]\n    assert ids == sorted(ids)\nfinally:\n    purge()\n=== END AC list-order-behavior ===\n\n## User Acceptance\n\n- None.\n\n## Guardrails\n\n- Tests never assume the store is empty; An empty title or author is refused\n    without touching the store, so a stored book always has both.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not title:\n        raise BookRejected(\"rejected: title is empty\")\n    if not author:\n        raise BookRejected(\"rejected: author is empty\")\n    return database.books.create(title=title, author=author)\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":25,"oldLines":3,"newStart":25,"newLines":12,"lines":["     if not author:","         raise BookRejected(\"rejected: author is empty\")","     return database.books.create(title=title, author=author)","+","+","+def list_books(database: Database) -> list[BookRow]:","+    \"\"\"Return every stored book in the order added, oldest first.","+","+    The order is enforced here, by ascending id, rather than trusted to the store's select, which","+    the generated persistence layer issues without an ORDER BY clause.","+    \"\"\"","+    return sorted(database.books.list(), key=lambda row: row.id)"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_013wmSo5JW1rA4ADVakEtWiC","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

Settings\n\nPROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent\n\n\ndef test_create_app_template_folder_is_app_server_templates():\n    app = create_app()\n\n    assert test_create_app_exposes_database_opened_from_configured_store(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n    store = tmp_path / \"wired.db\"\n    monkeypatch.setenv(\"DATABASE_URL\", f\"sqlite:///{store}\")\n    monkeypatch.delenv(\"DATABASE_PATH\", raising=False)\n\n    app = create_app()\n\n    assert isinstance(app.extensions[\"database\"], Database)\n\n\ndef test_create_app_does_not_create_store_file_at_startup(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n    store = tmp_path / \"lazy.db\"\n    monkeypatch.setenv(\"DATABASE_URL\", f\"sqlite:///{store}\")\n\n    create_app()\n\n    assert not store.exists()\n\n\ndef test_create_app_database_round_trips_through_configured_store(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n    store = tmp_path / \"roundtrip.db\"\n    monkeypatch.setenv(\"DATABASE_URL\", f\"sqlite:///{store}\")\n    app = create_app()\n    db = app.extensions[\"database\"]\n    db.execute_script((PROJECT_ROOT / \"schema.sql\").read_text())\n\n    created = db.books.create(title=\"Dune\", author=\"Frank Herbert\")\n    fetched = db.books.get(id=created.id)\n\n    assert fetched == created\n    assert store.is_file()\n    with sqlite3.connect(store) as connection:\n        assert connection.execute('SELECT title, author FROM \"books\"').fetchall() == [\n            (\"Dune\", \"Frank Herbert\")\n        ]\n\n\ndef test_create_app_registers_only_add_book_route_beside_static():\n    app = create_app()\n\n    endpoints = {rule.endpoint for rule in app.url_map.iter_rules()}\n\n    assert endpoints == {\"static\", Provides: books.create, books.list, books.get, books.delete.\nTable books: id INTEGER PK (autoincrement; defines insertion order), title TEXT NOT NULL, author TEXT NOT NULL.\n- FEATURE-BOOKS-001 books.create(title, author) -> BookRow(id, title, author). Write.\n- FEATURE-BOOKS-002 books.list() -> BookRow[] ascending id. Read. Generated select has no ORDER BY; callers needing order must sort by id.\n- FEATURE-BOOKS-003 books.get(id) -> BookRow. Read.\n- FEATURE-BOOKS-004 books.delete(id) -> BookDeleteResult(id). Write.\nAccess only via persistence.open_database(dsn) and db.books.<op>.
